title: Legacy CRM Data Model Package Inventory (DM v22.0)
summary: Comprehensive reference for the legacy CRM platform data model spanning 8 primary packages plus 5 connector packages, documenting the package structure, object types per package, standard object extensions, custom metadata types, custom settings, platform events, triggers, and validation rules that constitute the full data architecture.

findings.package_architecture: The data model is organized into 8 primary managed packages (the core platform and 7 extension packages) plus 5 connector packages for third-party integrations. Primary packages: the core CRM package (account management, call management, content delivery, territory management), extension package 1 (advanced analytics, activity plans, KAM features), extension package 2 (advanced compliance, consent management), extension package 6 (events management, speaker programs), extension package 8 (medical affairs, field medical), extension package 9 (order management, pricing), a quality/data connector package, and a digital engagement package. Connector packages provide integration with expense management, healthcare professional registries, order management systems, master data management platforms, and messaging platforms.
findings.standard_object_extensions: Five standard Salesforce objects are extended with custom fields across the platform: Account (HCP/HCO profiles, territory assignments, compliance attributes), ContentVersion (CLM presentation metadata, approval status), SurveyInvitation (compliance survey tracking), Territory2 (territory hierarchy and alignment), and User (role configuration, feature toggles, device assignments). These extensions follow the standard Salesforce pattern of adding custom fields to standard objects rather than creating parallel custom objects.
findings.custom_metadata_types: Each package defines custom metadata types for declarative configuration. The core package alone has 100+ custom metadata types covering: dependency injection container configuration, action definitions with context-based criteria, activity history display configuration, activity plan settings, address validation routing, admin console menu structure, affiliation role mappings, audit handlers, calendar event styling, call validation rules, compliance templates, content management, email configuration, event management, field coaching, geolocation services, integration settings, KOL management, mobile synchronization, order management, pricing rules, territory management, and user interface component configuration. Custom metadata follows a pattern where each type defines a specific feature's configurable behavior without requiring code changes.
findings.custom_settings: Hierarchical and list custom settings control runtime behavior at the org, profile, and user levels. Key areas: synchronization frequency and batch sizes, feature toggle flags, mobile device configuration parameters, offline data limits, UI display preferences, integration endpoint URLs, and logging configuration. The distinction between custom metadata (deploy-time configuration) and custom settings (runtime-adjustable parameters) follows a deliberate architectural separation.
findings.platform_events: Each package publishes platform events for asynchronous processing and cross-package communication. Event categories include: data synchronization events (record create/update/delete notifications), integration events (inbound/outbound data exchange triggers), user action events (call completion, sample drop, content interaction), compliance events (consent changes, regulatory submissions), and system events (error notifications, batch processing status). Platform events enable loose coupling between packages and support real-time mobile notification delivery.
findings.triggers_and_validation: Triggers are organized by package with the core package having the most (covering Account, Call, and related objects). Validation rules enforce data integrity within each package's domain: the core package validates call records and account data, extension package 1 validates activity plan records, extension package 6 validates event and speaker records, extension package 9 validates order and pricing records. Connector packages (expense management, messaging) have their own trigger logic for integration event handling. The OneKey connector additionally uses workflow rules for registry synchronization.
findings.record_types: Record types provide per-object behavioral polymorphism. The core package and extension package 8 make the heaviest use of record types. Record types drive page layout selection, business process assignment, and picklist value filtering — enabling a single custom object to serve multiple functional purposes across different user personas (sales representative vs. medical science liaison vs. key account manager).
findings.scale_characteristics: The complete data model spans approximately 2,700 pages of documentation covering 30+ functional domains. Object counts per package range from dozens of custom objects in the core package to focused sets of 5-15 objects in extension packages. The data model supports both online and offline operation, with synchronization metadata fields on most objects (sync timestamps, conflict resolution flags, mobile-specific identifiers) enabling bidirectional sync between server and mobile clients.

source: CRM DataModel - DM v22.0 (internal reference document, 2700+ pages)
